name: AI Expense Watchdog
value_proposition: Before any cancel, build a recurring-charge ledger from an export, show price-change formulas in plain text, and label possible overlaps as interpretation — the Blueprint never cancels a vendor.
persona: An owner or office manager who has not looked line by line at software and vendor spend for months, and who can export card, bank, or accounting transactions as CSV.
problem: Forgotten subscriptions, duplicate tools, and quiet price increases accumulate in card and bank statements. A generic chatbot will invent unused tools and a savings total.
workflow: 1. The person writes the keep list (vendors that must never be flagged for cancel), overlap-watch categories, and the minimum amount change worth listing. PERSON DECIDES: which vendors are essential and which categories to watch.

2. The person exports two or three months of card, bank, or accounting transactions as CSV with date, vendor, amount, and the file's date range. QuickBooks is optional only as a CSV export, not a live connection. PERSON DECIDES: which columns to keep. Remove card numbers, account numbers, and other columns the workflow does not need.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to upload the file, paste the rows as text, or not use AI for this data at all.
4. The person pastes the Recurring Ledger Prompt and their rules from the Keep List and Overlap Rules Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the CSV.

5. AI writes RECURRING LEDGER FIRST. It groups a vendor as recurring only when that exact vendor name appears in at least two months, lists one-time charges as NOT RECURRING, and skips keep-list vendors for cancel review.

6. For recurring vendors, AI fills visible change formulas from export amounts only (for example =39.00-29.00). A later higher amount is a CONFIRMED price change, not a savings figure. Possible duplicate tools are AI INTERPRETATION.
7. AI labels each point as CONFIRMED (from the CSV), AI INTERPRETATION (a possible overlap), or RECOMMENDED ACTION. It does not invent unused subscriptions or a savings total.

8. The person uses the Cancel Review Checklist and checks every CONFIRMED amount against the export row before touching a vendor account. PERSON DECIDES: whether to cancel, keep, or wait and re-export. The person cancels in the vendor's own site themselves. The Blueprint never cancels anything.
before: Recurring charges blur together. The owner guesses which tools overlap and sometimes cancels a tool the business still needs, or never reviews at all.
after: The owner sees a recurring ledger with visible formulas, one-time charges set aside, keep-list vendors skipped, and a short evidence-labelled list of what to confirm next. Nothing is cancelled automatically.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/ai-expense-watchdog using a fictional ten-row card export dated 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30, as of 2026-09-30. The keep list is ZoomMeet, the overlap-watch category is design tools, and the minimum change is 5.00. DesignHub Pro, CanvaLite Teams, and ZoomMeet are recurring; Harbor Office Supply is one charge; ZoomMeet is skipped for cancel review. The demo shows ledger formulas, labelled interpretation that DesignHub Pro and CanvaLite Teams may overlap, a fact check of DesignHub Pro against the export rows, and an ending that states the person cancels it. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The export: show the fictional card table of 10 rows whose vendor names include DesignHub Pro, CanvaLite Teams, ZoomMeet, and Harbor Office Supply. Show '2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30', '2026-09-30', 'ZoomMeet', 'design tools', and '5.00'. Label the table invented. State that no live card network, bank, QuickBooks, or Plaid account is attached.

Step 2 of 6 - Recurring ledger first: show the exact heading 'RECURRING LEDGER FIRST'. List DesignHub Pro, CanvaLite Teams, and ZoomMeet as recurring. List Harbor Office Supply as NOT RECURRING with text containing '84.00' and 'one charge'. List ZoomMeet as skipped for cancel review.

Step 3 of 6 - Visible formulas, then stop: show a ledger table. DesignHub Pro formula text '=39.00-29.00', result '10.00'. CanvaLite Teams formula text '=30.00-30.00', result '0.00'. ZoomMeet formula text '=15.99-15.99', result '0.00'. Show the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words, not as color or icon alone. Show AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'may overlap' and 'not a savings figure'. Show RECOMMENDED ACTION text containing 'confirm who uses' and 'Do not cancel from a guess.'.

Step 4 of 6 - Check the facts: open the DesignHub Pro CONFIRMED line with 29.00 and 39.00. A 'Check facts against the export row' button shows three rows (2026-07-03, 2026-08-03, 2026-09-03), each labelled with the text 'Matches', and the values 29.00, 39.00, and 39.00.

Step 5 of 6 - What a later run needs: show 'No new export was provided.', 'no usage column', ZoomMeet on the keep list, and the sentence 'Re-run next month with a new export. Do not cancel from a guess.'.

Step 6 of 6 - You cancel it: state the exact sentences 'You cancel it. The kit changes nothing.' and 'Do not cancel from a guess.' Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.

kit_contents.title: Expense Review Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for one review. It covers writing the keep list and overlap-watch categories, exporting two or three months of card, bank, or accounting transactions as CSV with date, vendor, amount, and the file's date range, treating QuickBooks as an optional CSV export only, checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading, and the rule that this is an export review, not a live connector. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Recurring Ledger Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that writes RECURRING LEDGER FIRST, groups a vendor as recurring only when it appears in at least two months, lists one-time charges as NOT RECURRING, skips keep-list vendors for cancel review, and labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. It forbids inventing unused tools, claiming savings, and cancelling.

kit_contents.title: Price Change and Overlap Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt used only after the ledger is built. It fills visible change formulas from export amounts, treats a later higher amount as a CONFIRMED price change not a savings figure, and labels possible overlaps as AI INTERPRETATION.

kit_contents.title: Keep List and Overlap Rules Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person sets essential vendors to never flag for cancel, overlap-watch categories, and the minimum amount to list as a price change. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the ledger prompt. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Recurring Ledger Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (vendor, jul, aug, sep, cadence, change_formula, change_result, keep_list) with fictional example rows and a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Cancel Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before cancelling anything. It confirms recurring vendors appear in at least two months, one-time charges were not called subscriptions, each CONFIRMED amount matches an export row, overlaps are labelled interpretation, no savings total was invented, and the person cancels in the vendor's own site themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Card Export
kit_contents.purpose: The same 10-row fictional CSV used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real financial data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling financial data in AI tools: review data settings, remove card and account numbers, do not invent savings, do not claim a tool is unused when the export has no usage column, and remember that nothing is cancelled automatically.

decision_rules: Write RECURRING LEDGER FIRST and apply it before any overlap guess, cancel suggestion, or savings language.
Use the export's own date range, not today's date. If the CSV has no date range, ask the person for it before building the ledger.
Group a vendor as recurring only when that exact vendor name appears in at least two months of the export. Show the months.
A charge that appears only once is NOT RECURRING. Show the reason 'one charge in the export'. Do not call it a subscription.
Skip any vendor on the keep list for cancel review. Show the reason 'on your keep list'.
If a remaining row is missing date, vendor, or amount, or the same vendor appears twice on the same date with different amounts, do not rank it. List it under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.
Do not claim a tool is unused. If the export has no usage column, write 'no usage column in the export' under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.
Leave every change formula visible as text (for example =39.00-29.00). A later higher amount is a CONFIRMED price change from the CSV, not a savings claim.
List a price change only when the later amount minus the earlier amount is at least the person's minimum.
Possible duplicate tools are AI INTERPRETATION. Do not merge similar vendor names. A possible overlap is not proof either tool can be cancelled.
Do not invent amounts, vendors, unused subscriptions, or savings totals. Do not treat a price change as money the business will get back.
On a later run, use a new export. If the person has not attached a new export, say that no new export was provided.
human_ai_boundary: AI groups recurring vendors from the export. The person decides which vendors are essential and which categories to watch.
AI writes RECURRING LEDGER FIRST and skips keep-list vendors for cancel review. The person decides whether a vendor stays on the keep list.
AI fills ledger formulas from export amounts and leaves the arithmetic visible. The person checks every CONFIRMED number against the export row before treating it as true.
AI labels CONFIRMED facts, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. The person decides whether a possible overlap is worth investigating.

AI never connects to a card network, bank, QuickBooks, or Plaid, never cancels a vendor, and never uploads the person's files to a third party. The person cancels in the vendor's own site, or decides not to.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person cancels it and that the kit changes nothing.
Atlas does not connect to a card network, bank, QuickBooks, Plaid, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.
Before pasting or uploading exports to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings and to remove card numbers, account numbers, and other columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste card numbers, bank account numbers, passwords, or tax IDs into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.
The kit tells the person not to cancel from a guess, not to invent unused tools, and not to treat a price change as a savings figure.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout. Fictional export amounts and confirmed differences are the only dollar figures.
required_data_tools: Card, bank, or accounting CSV export for two or three months with date, vendor, amount, and the file's date range
QuickBooks optional only as a CSV export, not a live connection
Spreadsheet (Google Sheets or Excel) so ledger formulas stay visible
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.
